_schema: One current record per exercise, oldest first. Read this index before generating or reviewing; update after publishing an exercise or reviewing a submission. The latest GitHub branch/README/source remains authoritative when validating details.

_fields.folder: Exact dated exercise folder; branch may differ from main
_fields.domain_or_topic: Brief topic for rotation and targeted revisits
_fields.difficulty: Integer 1-5, matching the exercise README (convert older scales explicitly)
_fields.submission_status: assigned | reviewed; reviewed means an attempt was evaluated, not necessarily accepted
_fields.completion_status: not_submitted | needs_revision | completed; only mark completed when acceptance criteria are met
_fields.outcome: pending | struggled | solid | mastered; diagnostic review label, independent of completion
_fields.notes: Concrete review findings, not assumed knowledge
_fields.key_learnings: Review takeaways offered to the learner; do not claim mastery without evidence
_fields.revisit: Whether a follow-up should address this concept
_fields.submission_branch: The reviewed branch name, if known
_fields.reviewed_on: YYYY-MM-DD when review occurred, if known

_generation_rules: Read this index first, then inspect the recent README/source/tests or reviewed branch as needed to verify details. Do not treat the ledger as a substitute for checking code when grading.
When a new dated folder is successfully pushed, append one assigned record with pending outcome and not_submitted completion_status. Never infer submission or completion merely from elapsed time.

When reviewing a submitted branch, update its record with review findings, one or two takeaways to practice, branch, review date, and completion_status. Only use completed after verified acceptance criteria; otherwise use needs_revision.

Rotate across code review, debugging, architecture tradeoffs, TypeScript modeling, and React state/performance; avoid the last two categories when practical. Work a revisit of a flagged concept into an upcoming exercise without automatically repeating the category every time.
Hold difficulty near 1/5 initially; raise gradually after multiple demonstrated solid or mastered reviews. Pending submissions alone do not prove readiness to increase difficulty.

log.domain_or_topic: notification external store and component lifecycle
log.notes: The reviewed branch passes the original 11 tests and improves subscription cleanup, but addNotification mutates the snapshot array with push; useSyncExternalStore may not notify React because the snapshot identity stays the same. A render regression test exposed this.
key_learnings: External-store updates must publish a new snapshot identity for useSyncExternalStore consumers.

log.domain_or_topic: notification variants and untrusted input boundary
log.notes: Revised submission passes all 13 tests and strict typechecking. Variant required fields, a parsing step, exhaustive row handling, and the exact expiration boundary are improved. A system notification can still carry conversationId through structural assignment, and raw API input is typed as already-valid base fields; runtime validation of malformed fields remains incomplete.
key_learnings: Narrowing by kind helps, but TypeScript's structural typing allows extra properties on existing variables unless forbidden fields are modeled or checked at the boundary.
Treat network values as unknown until the required and optional fields have been validated.
